import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Calculate effect sizes (mean difference in outcome groups)
    effect_sizes = []
    for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
        feat_vals = feats.x[:, i]
        y = feats.y
        mean_y1 = np.mean(feat_vals[y == 1])
        mean_y0 = np.mean(feat_vals[y == 0])
        effect_size = mean_y1 - mean_y0
        effect_sizes.append((effect_size, fid))
    
    # Sort by absolute effect size
    effect_sizes.sort(key=lambda x: abs(x[0]), reverse=True)
    
    # Look for potential drivers (features with large effect sizes)
    drivers = [fid for _, fid in effect_sizes[:MAX_DRIVERS]]
    
    # Remove near-duplicates based on correlation > 0.6
    corr_matrix = np.corrcoef(feats.x.T)
    to_remove = set()
    for i in range(len(feats.ids)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(feats.ids)):
            if abs(corr_matrix[i,j]) >= 0.6:
                to_remove.add(feats.ids[j])
    
    # Filter out near-duplicates
    drivers = [d for d in drivers if d not in to_remove]
    
    # If no strong associations found, return empty design
    if not drivers:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Select columns for regression (drivers only)
    columns = drivers
    
    # No products to keep model small
    products = ()
    
    # Simple weighted score: sum of driver effects
    loadings = {}
    for d in drivers:
        idx = feats.column(d)
        feat_vals = feats.x[:, idx]
        mean_y1 = np.mean(feat_vals[feats.y == 1])
        mean_y0 = np.mean(feat_vals[feats.y == 0])
        loadings[d] = mean_y1 - mean_y0
    
    return Design(drivers=tuple(drivers), columns=tuple(columns), products=products, loadings=loadings)
